catalog_quote: There is lexical prosody in Yuwan. That is, each root has its own prosodic pattern, and these patterns fall into three types. I. Falling after the penultimate mora of a phonological word II. Falling after the syllable including the second mora of a phonological word III. Rising at the final mora of a phonological word (If the falling position is located word-finally, then falling is realized after the penultimate mora.) In the following tables, both “H” (high pitch) and “L” (low pitch) are counted as a mora respectively. [...] This table shows that in order to determine the type II pitch pattern, it is necessary to count both syllables and morae. Most of the lexicon belonging to type II is realized with falling after the second mora, such as /sɨ.ka.ma.nu/ sɨkama=nu (morning=NOM) produced as HHLL and /məə.ra.bɨ.nu/ məərabɨ=nu (lady=NOM) produced as HHLLL. However, if the second syllable contains a vowel sequence, the falling occurs after the third mora, such as /hi.zjai.nu/ hizjai=nu (left=NOM) produced as HHHL, which means type II represents falling not after the second mora, but after the second syllable including the second mora.

At printed pp. 49-50 (pp. 50-51, confirmed with extracted text/-f 51), section 2.5 'Prosody', 2.5.1 'Three pitch patterns' reads exactly: 'There is lexical prosody in Yuwan. That is, each root has its own prosodic pattern, and these patterns fall into three types. I. Falling after the penultimate mora of a phonological word II. Falling after the syllable including the second mora of a phonological word III. Rising at the final mora of a phonological word (If the falling position is located word-finally, then falling is realized after the penultimate mora.)' followed by Table 20 (haa 'leaf' HL/HHL.., judai, haa 'teeth…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Yuwan has no stress accent; it has a lexical three-pattern (N-kei) pitch accent/word-tone system. Every root belongs to one of three classes whose pitch shape is computed over the phonological word (host + clitics) by mora count: Type I = pitch fall after the penultimate mora (HH…HL), Type II = fall after the syllable containing the second mora from the left (HHLL…), Type III = low throughout with a rise on the final mora (LL…LH). The class is lexical; the location of the pitch event within each class is predictable from the word edges.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described (no stress at all; the only sub-regularity is that words with an initial glottalized resonant or kˀw/kˀj show the Type II fall after the first mora, §2.5.2 p. 51).
new_statements.exceptions: Glottalized-initial words form a phonotactically conditioned subcategory of Type II with the fall after the first mora (p. 51); many tokens are realized with flat pitch so class membership is sometimes indeterminate (p. 52); compounds keep the pattern of the first stem; recent loans via Standard Japanese tend to Type I (p. 52). Of 207 nominals: I 48%, II 27%, III 25%. Niinaga 2010 (pp. 43-44) numbers the same three classes differently (1 = final-mora high, 2 = final-mora low, 3 = fall at the word boundary).
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the phonological word = grammatical word plus following clitics (§2.1.2, §2.5); Table 20 gives isolation forms and forms with =nu, =n, =gadɨ, showing the fall/rise moving with the clitics. Tone-bearing unit is the mora (long vowels/diphthongs count two morae). Lawrence 2018 (pp. 121 ff.) independently confirms the three-pattern system with c. 800 classified words.
new_statements.identity_note: The statement describes Yuwan (湯湾, Uken village, south-western Amami Ōshima), the variety Glottolog 5.1 uses as the Glottolog's most extensive description for sout2954 and files all Niinaga Yuwan works; Note that in Japanese dialectology 'southern Amami Ōshima' (奄美大島南部) more narrowly means Setouchi town (Koniya, Shodon/Kakeroma etc.); those dialects have a different, TWO-pattern word-tone system (Matsumori 2019 p. 5: '瀬戸内町の諸方言は二型アクセント体系を持つ'; Hayata 1996 p. 23 on Shodon: a word-tone language with phrase-final falling vs rising tones), whereas Yuwan has THREE lexical patterns. Uwano 2000 groups Uken village with Setouchi as the 'southern area' of the island, consistent with Glottolog's assignment. Either way the typological reading is the same: lexical N-pattern pitch accent (word tone), no stress accent.

tone_statements.quote: 諸鈍方言の１，２類の単語は、他のおおくの琉球列島諸方言、とりわけ、北琉球方言におけるぱあいと同様にacuteaccentをもつ。諸鈍方言のacuteaccentは下降調で、筋肉の弛緩とともにピッチが下降し、呼気流量も減少する。
tone_statements.translation: Shodon words of (Kindaichi) classes 1 and 2, as in many other Ryukyuan dialects and especially the Northern Ryukyuan ones, have the acute accent. The Shodon acute accent is falling: the pitch falls as the muscles relax and airflow decreases.
tone_statements.summary: Shodon: historical noun classes 1-2 carry the falling (acute) word tone; the falling type conditions loss of final high vowels (closed syllables).

tone_statements.citation: Niinaga, Yuto. 2014. A Grammar of Yuwan, a Northern Ryukyuan Language. PhD dissertation, University of Tokyo (doi:10.15083/00007642).
tone_statements.quote: 音調は ˹ ( 高音調の始まり ) と ˺ ( 高音調から低音調への下降の位置 ) で表示する。... 西古見方言の音調型は基本的に、高く始まり語末で下降する型と、低く始まり語末で上昇する型の二つに大別されるが、複合語においては (4) に示すように語中の形態素間の境界の前後から高くなる音調型もある。((4) の中の点 ( . ) は複合語内部の最大構成素の境界を表す標識である 。)
tone_statements.translation: Tone is indicated with ˹ (the beginning of high pitch) and ˺ (the position of the fall from high pitch to low pitch). ... The tone patterns of the Nishikomi dialect are basically divided into two: a pattern that begins high and falls at the end of the word, and a pattern that begins low and rises at the end of the word; but in compounds, as shown in (4), there is also a tone pattern in which pitch becomes high from around the boundary between word-internal morphemes. (The dot ( . ) in (4) marks the boundary of the major constituents inside the compound.)
tone_statements.locator: §1 はじめに, p. 155 and p. 156
tone_statements.summary: Two word-level tone patterns (high-start falling vs low-start rising) written with H-onset and H-to-L fall marks; compounds may rise at a morpheme boundary; ~1300 tone-marked nouns, verbs, adjectives.

tone_statements.citation: Karimata, Shigehisa 狩俣繁久. 1996. 鹿児島県大島郡瀬戸内町諸鈍方言のフォネーム（下） [The phonemes of the Shodon dialect, part 2]. 日本東洋文化論集 (琉球大学法文学部) 2: 1-57. hdl:20.500.12000/2292.
tone_statements.quote: 上村幸雄1983、上村幸雄1989ａの方法にならって諸鈍方言の単語のリズム＝アクセント的構造について概観する。[...] 諸鈍方言にはつぎにみられるようなリズム構造のタイプ〈すなわち、脚 [...] のタイプがあり、それぞれの脚ごとにacuteaccentとgraveaccentのふたつのタイプのアクセント型の対立がみられる。[...] 諸鈍方言のばあい、－音節語は短い音節の○ではなく、長い音節の○である。そのフォネーム構造はＣＶ：、あるいはＣＶＣである。ＣＶ：のばあい、graveaccent（上昇調）の単語については話者もその母音がながいと感じ、acuteaccent（下降調）については、その母音が短いと感じる話者がいらっしゃる。
tone_statements.translation: Following the method of Uemura 1983, 1989a I survey the rhythm-accent structure of Shodon words. [...] The Shodon dialect has the following types of rhythmic structure, i.e. foot types, and for each foot there is an opposition of two accent types, acute accent and grave accent. [...] In Shodon a monosyllabic word is not a short syllable but a long one (CV: or CVC). In the CV: case, for grave-accent (rising) words speakers feel the vowel is long, and for acute-accent (falling) words some speakers feel the vowel is short.
tone_statements.locator: pp. 1-3, §1 「諸鈍方言のリズム＝アクセント的構造」, Table 1 (表①); note 3 p. 22
tone_statements.summary: Shodon (Setouchi): two lexical word-accent (word-tone) types, acute = falling vs grave = rising, realized over feet of short/long syllables; no separate word stress (rhythmic strong/weak syllables are part of the foot description).

tone_statements.citation: Karimata, Shigehisa 狩俣繁久 (かりまたしげひさ). 1995. 鹿児島県大島郡瀬戸内町諸鈍方言のフォネーム（上） [The phonemes of the Shodon dialect, Setouchi town, Ōshima district, Kagoshima prefecture, part 1]. 日本東洋文化論集 (琉球大学法文学部紀要) 1: 1-23. Nishihara: University of the Ryukyus. hdl:20.500.12000/2290.
tone_statements.quote: There are three distinctive lexical pitch patterns in Yuwan: final mora high, final mora low, and a fall at the word boundary.
tone_statements.locator: sec. 2.5 'Prosody', p. 43; Table 7 'Examples of pitch patterns' on p. 44
tone_statements.summary: Yuwan (Uken): three-pattern lexical pitch accent, mora = TBU, phonological word (word+clitics) = domain.

tone_statements.citation: Karimata, Shigehisa, Kōichi Tomitaka, Akiko Nagamine & Yong-Gyu Kim かりまたしげひさ・冨高康一・長嶺明子・金庸珪. 1992. 鹿児島県大島郡瀬戸内町諸鈍方言における単語のリズム＝アクセント的構造について [On the rhythm-accent structure of words in the Shodon dialect, Setouchi]. In Uemura, Yukio 上村幸雄 (ed.), 琉球列島における音声の収集と研究 I (文部省重点領域研究「日本語音声における韻律的特徴の実態とその教育に関する総合的研究」琉球列島班研究成果報告書), 49-90. [Nishihara]: 「日本語音声」琉球列島班 / 沖縄言語研究センター.
tone_statements.quote: 屋鈍方言はモーラを韻律単位とする2型音調の方言と認められる。しかし、以下に示す如く、その具体的様相は多くの独立性の乏しいモーラの存在によって聊か複雑である。... 如上の調値は、次のような調類にまとめられる。... 調類～調値の関係規定は、a類：語句の第2モーラ以後を高にせよ。語に第2モーラが無ければ、語句の第1モーラ以後を高にせよ。b類：語句の第2モーラを高にせよ。語に第2モーラが無ければ、語句の第1モーラを降にせよ。
tone_statements.translation: The Yadon dialect is recognised as a two-pattern tone dialect with the mora as its prosodic unit. However, as shown below, its concrete shape is somewhat complicated by the presence of many morae of weak independence. ... The tone values above can be grouped into the following tone classes. ... The rules relating tone class to tone value are: class a: make the phrase high from its 2nd mora onward; if the word has no 2nd mora, make the phrase high from its 1st mora onward. class b: make the 2nd mora of the phrase high; if the word has no 2nd mora, make the 1st mora of the phrase falling.
tone_statements.locator: sec. 2-2, p. 20 first two sentences, and p. 22 above and below the tone-class table
tone_statements.summary: Yadon (Uken): two mora-based word-tone classes; a = high from 2nd mora on, b = 2nd mora high (fall if monomoraic). Verbs merge to one class, adjectives keep two. A 3-pattern reading is rejected (p25).

tone_statements.citation: Kasuga, Shōzō 春日正三. 1962. 請島方言の音韻 [The phonology of the Ukejima dialect]. 立正大学文学部論叢 14: 50-66. Risshō University. hdl:11266/2763.
tone_statements.quote: 諸鈍方言のアクセントは語形と密接なつながりがある。アクセントのない二音節名詞(語形は CVCV(V)) は、ほとんどの場合、二音節目の母音が長短の交替を持つ。 ... The symbol "^" after a word shows that it is atonic. ... But shapes ending with ..VCCV have a slightly falling pitch on the first vowel, followed by a rise to 3 on the last syllable (Uemura 1959, 1962). qapra^ (32) 'oil'
tone_statements.translation: [Japanese part:] The accent of the Shodon dialect is closely tied to word shape. Unaccented disyllabic nouns (shape CVCV(V)) in most cases have a long/short alternation of the second-syllable vowel. [rest is English]
tone_statements.locator: Japanese preface (序文) p. 1, under 名詞: 語形とアクセントとの関係.. p. 8 fn. 4.. p. 14 top, end of sec. 2.1.1
tone_statements.summary: Internal reconstruction of Shodon (Kakeroma). Words are accented vs unaccented/atonic (marked ^); pitch shapes given with level numbers, citing Uemura. Accent pages 12-13 not seen.

Adds class correspondence (classes 1-2 = falling type) to the two-type system of part 1.

sources.note: Analysis of Shodon (Kakeroma Is., Setouchi) noun prosody from Karimata et al. 1992 and Tomitaka 1993 data; p. 23: 'この方言が、句末下降と句末上昇の二つの声調（トーン）からなる単語声調言語である、ということは誰が見ても明瞭である' — a word-tone language with two tones, phrase-final falling vs phrase-final rising; pitch-assignment rules refer to the leftmost heavy syllable. sources.note: p. 5: '古仁屋方言をはじめとした瀬戸内町の諸方言は二型アクセント体系を持つ' — Koniya and the other Setouchi dialects have a two-pattern accent system: a 'falling type' (2nd mora from the start of the bunsetsu high, phrase ends falling) and a 'rising type' (two H peaks in 3+ mora phrases, phrase ends rising); classes correlate with historical tone series A vs B/C. pitch accent/word-tone, no stress statement. Relevant because Setouchi is the traditional 'southern Amami' area under ISO ams.

sources.note: Survey of Amami accent systems from the author's 200-village fieldwork: N-pattern (mostly two-pattern) accent systems dominate, multi-pattern systems scattered; double-peaked contours concentrate in Kikai and in southern Amami Ōshima (Uken village and Setouchi town); e.g. Shiba (Kakeroma, Setouchi) 'is basically a two-pattern accent system' (p. 44-45). No stress statement; Yuwan not treated individually.

tone.translation: Following the method of Uemura 1983, 1989a I survey the rhythm-accent structure of Shodon words. [...] The Shodon dialect has the following types of rhythmic structure, i.e. foot types, and for each foot there is an opposition of two accent types, acute accent and grave accent. [...] In Shodon a monosyllabic word is not a short syllable but a long one (CV: or CVC). In the CV: case, for grave-accent (rising) words speakers feel the vowel is long, and for acute-accent (falling) words some speakers feel the vowel is short.
tone.summary: Shodon (Setouchi): two lexical word-accent (word-tone) types, acute = falling vs grave = rising, realized over feet of short/long syllables; no separate word stress (rhythmic strong/weak syllables are part of the foot description).

sources.quote: 屋鈍方言はモーラを韻律単位とする2型音調の方言と認められる。しかし、以下に示す如く、その具体的様相は多くの独立性の乏しいモーラの存在によって聊か複雑である。... 如上の調値は、次のような調類にまとめられる。... 調類～調値の関係規定は、a類：語句の第2モーラ以後を高にせよ。語に第2モーラが無ければ、語句の第1モーラ以後を高にせよ。b類：語句の第2モーラを高にせよ。語に第2モーラが無ければ、語句の第1モーラを降にせよ。

sources.note: Yadon (Uken): two mora-based word-tone classes; a = high from 2nd mora on, b = 2nd mora high (fall if monomoraic). Verbs merge to one class, adjectives keep two. A 3-pattern reading is rejected (p25).

tone.quote: 屋鈍方言はモーラを韻律単位とする2型音調の方言と認められる。しかし、以下に示す如く、その具体的様相は多くの独立性の乏しいモーラの存在によって聊か複雑である。... 如上の調値は、次のような調類にまとめられる。... 調類～調値の関係規定は、a類：語句の第2モーラ以後を高にせよ。語に第2モーラが無ければ、語句の第1モーラ以後を高にせよ。b類：語句の第2モーラを高にせよ。語に第2モーラが無ければ、語句の第1モーラを降にせよ。
tone.locator: sec. 2-2, p. 20 first two sentences, and p. 22 above and below the tone-class table
tone.translation: The Yadon dialect is recognised as a two-pattern tone dialect with the mora as its prosodic unit. However, as shown below, its concrete shape is somewhat complicated by the presence of many morae of weak independence. ... The tone values above can be grouped into the following tone classes. ... The rules relating tone class to tone value are: class a: make the phrase high from its 2nd mora onward; if the word has no 2nd mora, make the phrase high from its 1st mora onward. class b: make the 2nd mora of the phrase high; if the word has no 2nd mora, make the 1st mora of the phrase falling.
tone.summary: Yadon (Uken): two mora-based word-tone classes; a = high from 2nd mora on, b = 2nd mora high (fall if monomoraic). Verbs merge to one class, adjectives keep two. A 3-pattern reading is rejected (p25).

But shapes ending with ..VCCV have a slightly falling pitch on the first vowel, followed by a rise to 3 on the last syllable (Uemura 1959, 1962). qapra^ (32) 'oil'

tone.quote: 近隣の方言では、（少なくとも歴史的には）母音削除がアクセントによって条件付けられていることが指摘されている（三石（1980：53）、かりまた（1996：12）参照）。請阿室方言において、共時的にも、母音削除はアクセントによって条件付けられており、アクセントが置かれた狭母音は削除されない、と分析する可能性もあるが、現時点ではアクセントに関する調査及び分析が十分でないため、この議論は別稿に譲る。 ... 今後の課題として、アクセント・イントネーションの記述、形態音韻論的交替の理論的分析がある。

tone.translation: For neighbouring dialects it has been pointed out that vowel deletion is (at least historically) conditioned by accent (see Mitsuishi 1980:53, Karimata 1996:12). For Ukeamuro too one could analyse vowel deletion as synchronically accent-conditioned, accented high vowels not deleting, but since investigation and analysis of the accent are at present insufficient we leave this discussion to another paper. ... Remaining tasks are the description of accent and intonation and a theoretical analysis of the morphophonological alternations.

sources.note: KAKEN summary (read): accent surveys of verbs/basic and conjugated forms in Sumiyo, Yamato, Uken and Setouchi covering 'most of the main villages' of southern Amami Ōshima; 'いずれの地点でも新しい成果が得られた。特に,住用村と大和村は従来,大部分が無アクセント地域とされていたが,すべてアクセント対立が存在することを確かめた。これは,音節構造の変化に伴うアクセント対立の発生という興味深い現象である' (all Sumiyo and Yamato dialects, formerly thought accentless, have accent distinctions, arising with syllable-structure change); part mentioned together with the Shiba (Setouchi) dialect in his 音声研究 2000 paper (in the works listed here); 'a consolidated data publication for these four municipalities is in prep…
